ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.claim: God used the accidental incident to teach the Prophet to focus on companions eager for reform, rather than pampering indifferent people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r3.anchor: used by the Almighty for the instruction and education of the Prophet (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r4.claim: The Prophet initially concentrated on Quraysh because he was directed to warn his near family, and their conversion could open Arabia to Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r4.anchor: as is evident from the following verse:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r5.claim: After Quraysh’s arrogance made reform unlikely, pursuing them cost time better spent educating poor believers, so the incident enabled a change in strategy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p173/r5.anchor: the time being wasted on them was at the cost of poor Muslims who had already embraced faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.claim: The Prophet’s devotion to persuading Quraysh leaders led him to neglect his own comfort and risk leaving little time to teach poor believers; he had assumed more than God required.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p175/r1.anchor: he had taken much more upon himself than the responsibility that was imposed upon him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r3.claim: Only God-fearing people who seek reform merit the Prophet’s attention and constitute his responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p176/r3.anchor: Only the God-fearing who have the urge to reform themselves are worthy of his attention

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.claim: The indifferent are absorbed in worldly pleasures and do not consider the afterlife, whereas those who fear meeting God are receptive; the Prophet pursued the former while neglecting the latter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.anchor: there are people who fear meeting God in the Hereafter

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.claim: Luxury and self-sufficiency signal rejection and readiness for disbelief and wrongdoing; affliction can purify, humble, and soften hearts, so the more deeply tried are more receptive to fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r2.anchor: الاستغناء والترف أمارة الإعراض وعدم القابلية والتهيؤ للكفر والفجور ، وإلى أن المصائب أمارة للطهارة والإقبال واستكانة القلوب

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.claim: Istaġnā is an antonym of ittaqā and appears near taqwā in 96:7; in 80:5 the positive counterpart is piety in 80:9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Das Verb wird hier offensichtlich als Antonym zu ittaqā (V. 5) gebraucht; auch in 96:7 steht istaġnā in der Nähe von taqwā

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r1.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the person considers himself independent of faith.

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says the person considers himself independent of God.

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r3.claim: Some take the word to mean becoming wealthy, but Rāzī rejects that sense here because the Prophet was not courting people for their wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : استغنى أثرى وهو فاسد ههنا ، لأن إقبال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يكن لثروتهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r4.claim: It is valid to say he felt self-sufficient through wealth, meaning that his riches made him think he needed neither faith nor the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#2/r4.anchor: ومن قال : أما من استغنى بماله فهو صحيح ، لأن المعنى أنه استغنى عن الإيمان والقرآن

STUDYQURAN:80:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r4.claim: Istaghna literally means self-sufficient and connotes seeing oneself as self-sufficient in relation to God.
STUDYQURAN:80:1/r4.anchor: Beyond need (v. 5) translates man istaghnā, which literally means

TAB-FULL:v24p107/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the self-sufficient people as Utba ibn Rabi'a and Shayba ibn Rabi'a.
TAB-FULL:v24p107/r3.anchor: جميعا عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {أما من استغنى} [عبس: 5] قال: عتبة بن ربيعة وشيبة بن ربيعة

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.claim: The proposed honorific reading of the switch from third to second person does not fit the direct address that follows, whose rebuke is stronger and has no conciliatory intimacy.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائمه الخطاب في قوله بعد { أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى }

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r2.claim: According to al-Rāghib, ghina, istighnāʾ, taghannī, and taghānī are synonymous.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r2.anchor: الغنى والاستغناء والتغني والتغاني بمعنى على ما ذكره الراغب

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r3.claim: The self-sufficient person is the wealthy one whose status and grandeur in others' eyes foster arrogance toward the truth.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r3.anchor: من تلبس بالغنى ولازمه التقدم والرئاسة والعظمة في أعين الناس والاستكبار عن اتباع الحق

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.claim: The rebuked pattern is that the Prophet attends to wealthy people who scorn the truth, unconcerned whether they purify themselves, while neglecting the person earnestly seeking purification and fearing God.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.anchor: أنك تعتني وتقبل على من استغنى واستكبر عن اتباع الحق وما عليك أن لا يزكى وتتلهى وتعرض عمن يجتهد في التزكي وهو يخشى

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.claim: The verses do not identify the Prophet as the person who frowned; the report leaves its subject unnamed, and the described conduct is incompatible with his character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r2.anchor: وليست الآيات ظاهرة الدلالة على أن المراد بها هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بل خبر محض لم يصرح بالمخبر عنه

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.speaker: المرتضى
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.claim: Al-Murtada is cited for the judgment that attending to the wealthy and neglecting the poor does not resemble the Prophet's noble character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r3.anchor: ثم الوصف بأنه يتصدى للأغنياء ويتلهى عن الفقراء لا يشبه أخلاقه الكريمة كما عن المرتضى رحمه الله

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.claim: The Prophet had already been praised for magnificent character in Surat Nun, revealed after the first revelation; this chronology makes a later rebuke for such conduct implausible.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r4.anchor: وقد عظم الله خلقه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذ قال

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.claim: Early Meccan commands to warn close kin and lower one's wing to believers further conflict with attributing disdain for the believing poor to the Prophet.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r5.anchor: فأمره بخفض الجناح للمؤمنين والسورة من السور المكية

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.claim: Early commands forbid longing for worldly goods, require gentleness toward believers, and direct the Prophet to proclaim and turn away from polytheists.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r6.anchor: وكذا قوله لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم ولا تحزن عليهم واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين

TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.claim: Preferring a rich person's wealth over a poor person's piety by turning away from the poor is rationally ugly and contrary to noble human character, even without an explicit prohibition.
TABATABAI:80:1-16/r7.anchor: قبح عقلي مناف لكريم الخلق الإنساني لا يحتاج في لزوم التجنب عنه إلى نهي لفظي

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.claim: The claim that the act became sinful only after this moment's prohibition is unsupported; even absent a revealed prohibition, reason judges it ugly and incompatible with the Prophet's praised character.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن دعوى أنه تعالى لم ينهه إلا في هذا الوقت تحكم ممنوع، ولو سلم فالعقل حاكم

TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.claim: A report from al-Sadiq in al-Majma says the passage concerned an Umayyad man with the Prophet who recoiled, frowned, and turned away when Ibn Umm Maktum arrived; God recounted and condemned it.
TABATABAI:80:1-16#2/r2.anchor: أنها نزلت في رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فجاء ابن أم مكتوم

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r10.claim: The one who considers himself self-sufficient is a prominent, wealthy person among his people.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r10.anchor: أي من كان عظيما في قومه واستغنى بالمال

BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r5.claim: The particle ammā marks a contrast; the person who considers himself independent rejects faith and the knowledge and insights contained in the Qur'an.
BURSEVI:v10p258#2/r5.anchor: {أما} للتفضيل {من استغنى} عن الإيمان وعما عندك من العلوم

THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.claim: Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked for instruction while the Prophet addressed Quraysh leaders; the Prophet turned from him, thinking the elite might reject a following of blind, poor, and enslaved people.
THALABI:v10p130#3/r2.anchor: أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213/r1.claim: Ata says the person seeks independence from faith.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213/r2.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say he considers himself independent of God; the word is also glossed as being wealthy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي (¬3)، ومقاتل (¬4): استغنى عن الله في نفسه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r4.claim: “One who deems himself self-sufficient” means someone made wealthy.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:1-5/r4.anchor: { أما من استغنى } أثرى من المال.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r7.claim: The translation “one who considers himself wholly self-sufficient” describes the typical wealthy Meccan notables and tribal chiefs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r7.anchor: “Kendini her bakımdan ihtiyaçsız gören” diye çevirdiğimiz 5. âyet Mekke’nin ileri gelen zenginlerinin ve kabile reislerinin hâkim karakterini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r8.claim: Proud of their wealth and followers, these leaders persisted in disbelief and claimed or acted as if they did not need guidance from God and His Messenger.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:1/r8.anchor: mal ve adamlarının çokluğu sebebiyle büyüklük taslayarak inkârcılıkta devam ediyor, Allah ve peygamberinin kendilerine doğru yolu göstermelerine ihtiyaçlarının olmadığını söylüyor

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r10.claim: One who feels self-sufficient in himself has thereby become self-sufficient from God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r10.anchor: أما من استغنى عن نفسه فإنه استغنى عن الله

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r11.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r11.claim: An alternative gloss takes the self-sufficient person to be one who has become wealthy through his property.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r11.anchor: ويقال : استغنى بما له فأنت له تصدى

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.claim: The whole passage is a reproach directed to the Prophet on behalf of the poor.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.anchor: وهذا كله من قبيل العتاب معه لأجل الفقراء

ITQAN:v4p394/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r7.claim: The self-sufficient man is Umayya ibn Khalaf, or, in another report, ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa.
ITQAN:v4p394/r7.anchor: 5763 ﴿ أما من استغنى ﴾ هو أمية بن خلف وقيل هو عتبة بن ربيعة

SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says God commanded the Prophet to keep company with the poor.
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمجالسة الفقراء

SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says God urged the Prophet to honor the poor.
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمجالسة الفقراء وحثه على تعظيمهم

SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says God forbade the Prophet from loving the wealthy.
SULAMI:v2p373#3/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : أمر الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بمجالسة الفقراء وحثه على تعظيمهم ونهاه عن محبة الأغنياء

ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p283#2/r1.claim: The addressee attends to the person who considers himself self-sufficient.

ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n2/r1.claim: The self-sufficient person is, in Asad's reading, someone who feels no need for divine guidance, especially the arrogant pagan chiefs addressed by the Prophet.
ASAD-NOTES:80:3#n2/r1.anchor: who does not feel the need of divine guidance: a reference to the arrogant pagan chieftains

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.claim: ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.anchor: There is no basic difference between the central theme of both sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.claim: Though the Prophet is addressed in the rebuke, its intended target is the haughty leaders who ignore his message and want poor companions excluded to secure their own attendance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r3.anchor: Although the Prophet (sws) is addressed, yet the direction of this stern address is towards these supercilious people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is to teach those who come eagerly, including devoted companions, rather than pamper absent leaders; he is not accountable for those who refuse to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r4.anchor: His real responsibility is to educate and instruct only those who come to him enthusiastically.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r1.claim: The one who considers himself independent is indifferent to faith and to the knowledge and guidance contained in the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r1.anchor: أي عن الإيمان وعما عندك من العلوم والمعارف التي ينطوي عليها القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that unbelief makes him feel no need for guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r2.anchor: وفي معناه ما قيل استغنى لكفره عما يهديه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r3.claim: A further view takes the phrase to mean a wealthy person; Alusi objects that poverty is not mentioned as the contrast, though he points to an answer later in the discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p40#2/r3.anchor: وقيل أي وأما من كان ذا ثروة وغنى وتعقب بأنه لو كان كذلك لذكر الفقر في مقابله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the self-sufficient person relies on his wealth and feels independent of God and faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: عن الله وعن الإيمان بما له من المال.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r5.claim: The person regards himself as self-sufficient.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r5.anchor: { أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى } تتعرض له بالإقبال عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r14.claim: The self-sufficient person is one who sought and acquired wealth, whether or not he fears God or came seeking guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p323/r14.anchor: طلب الغنى وهو المال والثورة فوجده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.claim: Ammā means ‘whatever may occur’; whenever a self-sufficient person exists, the Prophet turns to him, with the conditional attachment exaggerating his persistent attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r10.anchor: تقدم الكلام على { أما } في سورة النازعات أنها بمعنى : مهما يكن شيء ، فقوله : { أما من استغنى } تفسيره مهما يكن الذي استغنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r11.claim: Istighnāʾ is counting oneself self-sufficient in a matter, inferred from speech, action, or knowledge; the added letters convey supposition, and the word often signals pride and confidence in one’s power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r11.anchor: والاستغناء : عد الشخص نفسه غنيا في أمر يدل عليه السياق قول ، أو فعل أو علم ، فالسين والتاء للحسبان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r12.claim: The referent is one who considers himself not in need of the Prophet’s guidance and declines it; the response implies he sees no objection but does not need it. This is not a wealthy person contrasted with a poor one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p106/r12.anchor: فالمراد ب { من استغنى } هنا : من عد نفسه غنيا عن هديك بأن أعرض عن قبوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r1.speaker: سلف المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r1.claim: The most widely transmitted early-exegete identification of the man to whom the Prophet presented the Qur’an is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r1.anchor: على أشهر الأقوال المروية عن سلف المفسرين الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي كما تقدم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.claim: Ammā means ‘whatever may occur’; whenever a self-sufficient person exists, the Prophet turns to him, with the conditional attachment exaggerating his persistent attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r10.anchor: تقدم الكلام على { أما } في سورة النازعات أنها بمعنى : مهما يكن شيء ، فقوله : { أما من استغنى } تفسيره مهما يكن الذي استغنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r11.claim: Istighnāʾ is counting oneself self-sufficient in a matter, inferred from speech, action, or knowledge; the added letters convey supposition, and the word often signals pride and confidence in one’s power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r11.anchor: والاستغناء : عد الشخص نفسه غنيا في أمر يدل عليه السياق قول ، أو فعل أو علم ، فالسين والتاء للحسبان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r12.claim: The referent is one who considers himself not in need of the Prophet’s guidance and declines it; the response implies he sees no objection but does not need it. This is not a wealthy person contrasted with a poor one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#6/r12.anchor: فالمراد ب { من استغنى } هنا : من عد نفسه غنيا عن هديك بأن أعرض عن قبوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r1.speaker: سلف المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r1.claim: Most reports from early exegetes identify the affluent man whom the Prophet addressed with the Qur’an as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r1.anchor: على أشهر الأقوال المروية عن سلف المفسرين الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he considered himself independent of God and faith because of his wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس استغنى عن الله وعن الإيمان بماله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the person who felt self-sufficient as ʿUtba and Shayba.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p27#4/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد أما من استغنى عتبة وشيبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.claim: The self-sufficient person is the rich man whom the Prophet approached in hope of guidance, though he was not accountable if the man failed to purify himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r3.anchor: أي: أما الغني فأنت تتعرض له لعله يهتدي،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.claim: God directs the Prophet to warn everyone equally, without favoring the eminent over the weak, rich over poor, masters over slaves, men over women, or adults over children; God guides whom He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.anchor: ومن هاهنا أمر الله عز وجل رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا يخص بالإنذار أحدا، بل يساوي فيه بين الشريف والضعيف، والفقير والغني، والسادة والعبيد،

JISHUMI:v10p7281/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r10.claim: This is a rebuke for attending to wealthy people while neglecting the poor; istaghna means becoming rich, with money and standing.
JISHUMI:v10p7281/r10.anchor: (أما من استغنى) هذا عتاب حين اششغل بالأغنياء عن الفقراء، واستغنى: أثرى وصار غنيا ذا مال وجاه

MUJAHID:v2p730#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p730#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p730#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the person who considers himself self-sufficient as a Qurayshi man, Umayya ibn Khalaf.
MUJAHID:v2p730#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ أما من استغنى ﴾ يعني رجلا من قريش وأمية بن خلف

MUQATIL:80:1-7/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r6.claim: The person who considers himself self-sufficient from God is Umayya ibn Khalaf.
MUQATIL:80:1-7/r6.anchor: عن الله في نفسه يعني أمية بن خلف

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#3/r1.claim: The one who considers himself self-sufficient is wealthy in money.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ أما من استغنى ﴾ أى منكان غنيا بالمال

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r1.claim: “Whoever considers himself independent” is a person with wealth and riches.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أما من استغنى } أي كان ذا ثروة وغنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r1.claim: The apparent sense of the self-sufficient person is someone wealthy; al-Kalbi says independent of God, and another view says independent of faith in God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r1.anchor: أما من استغنى: ظاهره من كان ذا ثروة وغنى. وقال الكلبي: عن الله. وقيل: عن الإيمان بالله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that taking the word as material wealth does not suit the station of prophethood; if intended, the contrast would be with a poor and lowly person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r2.anchor: وكونه بمعنى الثروة لا يليق بمنصب النبوة، ويدل على ذلك أنه لو كان من الثروة لكان المقابل

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.claim: In another account, ʿAʾisha says the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktum came; the Prophet turned away, and the quoted passage was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مجلس من ناس من وجوه قريش منهم أبو جهل بن هشام وعتبة بن ربيعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r7.claim: استغنى means that the person considers himself independent because of his wealth.
